# Additions to Esther Chapter 1 (Addition A) — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Additions to Esther A | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADE_001_page_001.jpg

---

*[Addition A: Mordecai's prophetic dream and his discovery of the assassination plot against the king. This section opens the Greek Esther, before the events of Hebrew Esther 1.]*

**1** It was the second year of the reign of Artaxerxes the Great. On the first day of Nisan, a man named Mordecai — son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, of the tribe of Benjamin — had a dream.

**2** Mordecai was a Jew living in the city of Susa, a man of standing who held a position in the royal court.

**3** He was among the exiles whom Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had carried away from Jerusalem when he took Jeconiah, king of Judea, captive.

**4** And this is what he dreamed: There were voices, and uproar, and thunder — earthquakes and violent chaos across the whole earth.

**5** Then two enormous dragons appeared, both of them poised and ready to fight; and a tremendous roar came out of them.

**6** At that roar, every nation in the world armed itself for war — to march against the nation of the righteous.

**7** It was a day of darkness and shadow — anguish, distress, and overwhelming disaster over all the earth.

**8** The whole nation of the righteous was thrown into panic, dreading the destruction closing in on them; they braced themselves for death.

**9** And they cried out to God. From their cry, what had been no more than a tiny trickle of water rose up and became a vast, surging river.

**10** Light broke through. The sun came up. The lowly were lifted up, and they swept away the mighty.

**11** When he woke from the dream and the visions, Mordecai turned everything over in his mind, trying to make sense of it all.

**12** Around that same time, Mordecai was on duty in the palace courtyard alongside Gabatha and Tharra, two of the king's eunuchs who were responsible for guarding the court.

**13** He overheard them plotting and looked into what they were planning — and discovered that they were preparing to assassinate King Artaxerxes. He reported this to the king immediately.

**14** The king had both eunuchs questioned; they confessed, and they were taken away for execution.

**15** The king had the whole affair put on record.

**16** Mordecai also wrote down his own account of these events.

**17** The king appointed Mordecai to a permanent position in the court and rewarded him with gifts in recognition of what he had done.
